extracted.intended_audience: partner organizations' communications and design teams (United Way affiliates, corporate & community partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Brand and partner usage guidelines for United Way: rules and standards for logo, color, typography, photography, partner lockups, messaging, and accessibility to ensure consistent, on-brand communications across print and digital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary logo composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary logo consists of the logo symbol (the Circle of Hope) and the logotype (the name set in customized type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circle of Hope includes the rainbow of hope, the hand support, and the person symbolizing humanity. The symbol should always appear in its entirety and never be deconstructed. The symbol has been repositioned and re-rendered for greater utility and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo structure (holding shape removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo symbol and logotype have been removed from the rectangular holding shape to better convey an open, inclusive and dynamic approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By repositioning and re-rendering the symbol, refreshing the logotype and removing the holding shape, the logo is optimized for small spaces and digital media. See pages 36–38 for localization guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred logo arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Our horizontal logo is the preferred version; the vertical logo works best for vertical layouts to optimize space and legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose horizontal for most contexts; use vertical where layout requires it to preserve legibility and space optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full logo vs. icon-only usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the full logo in all contexts except for small spaces (e.g., favicon or social media icon); in those small spaces the logo symbol (icon) may be used on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to page 15 for additional details on icon-only usage and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo clear space
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the logo clear of competing text, images and graphics by maintaining a minimum clear space equal to the height of the "U" of the logo on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided elements/diagrams as a guide to determine space around each logo placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo minimum size
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the logo legible by always using it at widths equal to or greater than specified minimums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizontal logo minimums: 2.0" for print and 200px for digital. Vertical logo minimums: 1.0" for print and 100px for digital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner logo lockups — how to reference
rubrics_metrics.description: How to describe strategic relationships in text when referencing partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe relationships as "A community partner of United Way" or "A corporate partner of United Way". Strategic relationships are external organizations with whom United Way works to achieve shared strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner logo lockups — visualization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to visually lock up partner logos with the United Way logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lock up partners' logos with United Way; where possible the United Way logo should lead. Keep the height of the partner logo equal to the height of the United Way logotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color palette usage and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only the colors chosen as part of the brand; primary colors (one, two or all three) should be applied across communications unless in a black-and-white context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary colors are derived from the logo symbol (blue, red, and gold) and each has four shades to provide dimension and dynamism. Maintain consistency across communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color values and approved shades
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and secondary brand colors have specific screen (RGB/hex) and print (CMYK/Pantone) values that must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided include Blue #0044B5 (R:0 G:68 B:181 / C:93 M:78 Y:0 K:0 / Pantone 2728 C), Red #FD372C (R:253 G:55 B:44 / C:0 M:91 Y:88 K:0 / Pantone Bright Red C), Gold #FFBA00, and many secondary/tertiary colors with exact values — use the listed values for accurate reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible color combinations & WCAG compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use approved text/background color combinations that meet WCAG 2.1 contrast standards (AA or AAA as indicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines list specific AAA and AA compliant combinations (e.g., Blue+White AAA, Gold+DK. Blue AAA). Use an online tool such as the Adobe Color Contrast Analyzer to check contrast ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand typography — fonts and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified brand fonts and their intended roles: Antonio for headlines, Palanquin for body copy and secondary headlines, Noto as an alternate for non-Latin scripts, and Monte Carlo (MonteCarlo Script) for special applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antonio is an all-uppercase headline font available on Google Fonts; Palanquin is optimized for legibility for body copy; Noto should be used where Antonio/Palanquin are unavailable for a language. Arial may be used when brand fonts cannot be installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography hierarchy and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the prescribed type treatments to establish a consistent messaging hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Headlines — Antonio Bold; Sub-headlines — Palanquin SemiBold; Body copy — Palanquin Regular; Pull quotes — Palanquin Bold. Apply these roles to create clear and compelling messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Italics are not recommended because they appear disruptive with the headline font (Antonio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If italics are absolutely necessary, use the italics of the alternate brand font (Noto) rather than Antonio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special use font (script) restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monte Carlo Script is a special-use font reserved for events and collateral that require a more sophisticated style (e.g., fundraising galas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Monte Carlo Script only for those special applications; it is not for general body or headline use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography should be community-rooted and responsive, highlighting people in action to express the brand promise, pillars and personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure images are engaging, energizing and elevating; showcase people connecting to their community and each other. Trust and transparency are key — do not substitute AI-generated photography or people-based illustrations for place-based, people-focused imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography — items to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific photographic anti-patterns to avoid to maintain an authentic look and feel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use: 1) photos that are out of focus; 2) photos with unnatural or extreme filters/effects; 3) photos that are overly posed; 4) photos on blank backgrounds/silhouetted and lacking context; 5) images of low resolution or poor quality; 6) photos that are overly busy or complex in composition; 7) AI-generated images or people-based illustrations. Add captions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo captions
rubrics_metrics.description: When using captions, they should provide context and follow prescribed alignment/placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions should be left-aligned and appear below the photo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved lockups and clear-space application
rubrics_metrics.description: Use approved horizontal/vertical lockups and follow provided clear-space diagrams to determine spacing around each logo placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved lockups and clear-space diagrams are provided in the guidelines; follow them to ensure correct spacing and alignment.
